newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Suzhou Goods 1996 net leaps on portfolio.
newsitem.headline: Suzhou Goods 1996 net leaps on portfolio.

text.p: China's Suzhou Goods Group Co Ltd on Wednesday reported a 414.1 percent rise in 1996 net profit, much of it coming from investment in shares and futures.

Based on Chinese accounting rules, net profit was 140.1 million yuan in 1996 compared with 27.2 million in 1995, but turnover dropped 22.1 percent to 742.4 million in 1996 from 952.6 million in 1995, the company said in its annual report.
More than 130 million yuan of the firm's 140 million yuan net profit came from the company's investments in the stock and futures markets, the report said.
The company, which sells cars, chemicals and coal, gained 70 million yuan from futures trading and more than 60 million yuan from investments in the stock markets, it said.
"This kind of business is not very stable as most earnings came from risky investments," said an analyst with Shenzhen J & A Securities.
Suzhou's share price rose 0.16 yuan to close at 24.93 yuan on Wednesday.

The company said its turnover was 25.8 percent short of target because of "risk-reduction policies", which reduced the scale of spot trading, as well as a lacklustre car market and weak demand for commercial properties.
Earnings per share rose to 1.16 yuan in 1996 from 0.27 yuan the year earlier, the company said, adding it would make a 10-for-10 bonus issue as a dividend based on 1996 profit.

It said it was also planning to make a three-for-10 rights issue, tentatively priced at between 5.0 yuan and 8.0 yuan per share, and channel the funds into stakes in financial institutions, property and a supermarket chain.
It will present the dividend and rights plans at a shareholders' meeting on April 3.
